# Assets, levels, and packaging

`karty.toml` supports this exact project asset surface:

```toml
[assets.theme]
source = "ui/theme.toml"

[[assets.texture]]
name = "ui.panel"
source = "assets/textures/ui-panel.png"
profile = "interface" # optional; defaults to sprite
keep = false           # optional: retain despite static stripping

[[assets.font]]
role = "display"      # body, display, mono; each at most once
source = "assets/fonts/title.otf"

[[assets.layout]]
source = "ui/layouts/window.ui" # build-time shell, no runtime name

[[assets.ui]]
name = "ui.inventory" # unique runtime UI asset name
source = "ui/views/inventory.ui"
```

`[project]` requires `name`; `compiler` is `tinygo` (default) or `go`.
`[project.resolution] width/height` default to 960×540 and must be positive.
`[sdk] version` pins the SDK. Texture names/sources are confined and unique;
names cannot begin `karty.`. Texture sources must be regular files. SDK 0.11
profiles are `sprite`, `interface`, `environment`; each uses the SDK-pinned PNG
processor.

Levels are `levels/<name>/level.toml`. A level can declare textures/UI by the
same logical rules and optional `[theme] source`. Game assets embed in
`game.kart`; level data/assets/UI embed in that level's `.kld` and are valid only
while its handle is mounted. Releasing a handle removes its entities, textures,
and UI state.

The build traces typed texture/UI/layout/theme-image/font references. Unused
game assets strip unless `keep = true`; level assets remain scoped to their
level. `dist/raw/asset-report.json` reports retention, sizes, processor cache,
and stripped candidates. It is diagnostic output, not a runtime catalog.

Only cartridges, host/shell runtime files, and diagnostics stage. Source PNGs,
fonts, theme TOML, UI files, global catalogs, and loose browser asset URLs are
not runtime resources. Metadata is embedded in each `.kart`/`.kld`.
